abstract: Selective autophagy receptors recognize and recruit harmful intracellular components to autophagosomes for degradation, and their dysfunction is linked to neurodegeneration, metabolic disorders, and cancer. Here, we identified TNFAIP3 interacting protein 1 (TNIP1) as an aggrephagy receptor implicated in neurodegenerative diseases. TNIP1 accumulated at polyubiquitinated protein aggregates upon proteotoxic stress. Genetic depletion of TNIP1 reduced protein aggregate clearance and increased axonal degeneration under proteotoxic stress. Mechanistically, TNIP1 enhanced protein aggregate clearance by assembling aggrephagy receptors, such as SQSTM1/p62 and TAX1BP1, onto protein aggregates. Gene expression analysis revealed that TNIP1 expression levels are reduced in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) with TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) inclusion pathology. Additionally, an ALS-associated TNIP1 mutant exhibited impaired association with TDP-43 aggregates and failed to rescue their autophagy-mediated degradation. These findings establish TNIP1 as an aggrephagy receptor and reveal its potential role as a therapeutic target for ALS and other proteinopathies.
